title: 1994 AMC 8 Problem 16
statement: The perimeter of one square is \(3\) times the perimeter of another square. The area of the larger square is how many times the area of the smaller square?

solutions.text:
A square’s perimeter is proportional to its side, so the larger square has side length \(3\) times the smaller one.

Area is the side squared, so the larger area is \(3^2 = 9\) times the smaller.

Thus, the correct answer is E .
hints: If the perimeter is \(3\) times as large, the side length is also \(3\) times as large
Area scales as the square of the ratio of side lengths
